title: How much room a room gets
question:
**Provisionally answered for the farmhouse** (CEO, 2026-09-15: 3x2 outside, 6x3 inside — a doubling across and a half again down). This card is what is left: whether that number holds for the coop and for everything after it.

Under P-18 a building's inside is its outside multiplied by a whole number — the number has to be whole or sixteen-pixel art shimmers and the yard behind it squashes. The farmhouse is 3x2 on the farm, so it can hold a 6x4, a 9x6 or a 12x8 room. The coop is 2x2, so 4x4, 6x6 or 8x8.

No room but the farmhouse's exists, so these panels are drawn rather than photographed — but every piece in them is the game's own art at the size the game draws it, which is the point: a bed is 16x32 and takes two whole tiles, a farmer's cell is 48x48. What the pictures show is how much floor is left once the things that have to be in the room are in it.

For reference, her room today is 10x7 and nobody has called it cramped.

The catch is that this is not only a question about floor. The same number sets how hard the farm magnifies behind the walls, so a bigger room is also a smaller view out — see the Q-108 sheet, where three times already reduces the yard to about one tile a side. If Q-108 goes to the backdrop option the two come apart and this is a free choice; if it goes to registered dilation, every step up here is paid for out of the window.
why_now: It is the one number in P-18 that is not forced, it sets the art budget for every interior the game ever has, and it is coupled to Q-108 — so the two want ruling together.

options.label: Two times
options.detail: A 6x4 farmhouse room and a 4x4 coop. The bed eats a quarter of the house and the hen most of the coop; this is close to the cramped room P-18 was written to fix. What it buys is the best view out under Q-108(a) — about two outside tiles a side.

options.label: Three times (Recommended)
options.detail: A 9x6 farmhouse room and a 6x6 coop. Both are comfortably furnishable and the house lands just under the 10x7 she already has, so nothing about today's room gets worse. The view out under Q-108(a) is roughly one tile a side, which is where that option starts to look thin.

options.label: Four times
options.detail: A 12x8 farmhouse room and an 8x8 coop. Bigger than anything the game has content for — the panels read as empty rather than spacious, and an empty room is a room that needs furnishing before it is worth entering. Under Q-108(a) the yard is gone entirely.

options.label: Per building, not one number
options.detail: Let each building carry its own multiplier: the farmhouse at three, the coop at two, a future barn at four. Nothing in P-18 requires one number for all of them, and it means a hen house never has to be as big as a home. The price is that there is no single answer to how magnified the yard is, so Q-108's treatment has to hold up across the whole range.

options.label: The farmhouse's own answer, everywhere (6x3 from 3x2)
options.detail: Take the ruling already given and make it the rule: a room is its footprint doubled across and half again down. The coop's 2x2 becomes 4x3. Consistent, and it keeps the yard readable through every wall — but 4x3 is a small coop, and the half-again is the axis that costs integer scaling.
